message.content:
We want to evaluate
\[
S=\sum_{k=1}^{p-2} k^{-1}(k+1)^{-1}\pmod p.
\]

Use the identity
\[
\frac{1}{k(k+1)}=\frac{1}{k}-\frac{1}{k+1}.
\]
Thus
\[
S=\sum_{k=1}^{p-2}\left(\frac{1}{k}-\frac{1}{k+1}\right).
\]
This is a telescoping sum:
\[
S=\frac11-\frac{1}{p-1}.
\]
Modulo \(p\),
\[
p-1\equiv -1 \pmod p,
\]
so
\[
\frac{1}{p-1}\equiv -1 \pmod p.
\]
Therefore
\[
S\equiv 1-(-1)=2 \pmod p.
\]

The answer is \(\boxed{2}\).
